findings.title: A failed merge-base is reported as "no source changed"
findings.fix: on a failed merge-base or git diff, print one line such as `project docs: not checked (<reason>)`. Use the repo's default branch instead of a literal `main`. Keep the close from failing.

sources.situation: the project's default branch is `master` or `trunk`, or `nio/<slug>` is missing (a renamed or deleted branch, or a shallow CI clone). `git merge-base main ...` exits non-zero. `records.git` discards the exit code, so `base` is "" and the function returns `[]`. A ValueError from `git diff` is swallowed the same way. The close prints nothing. A dev who added `httpx` sees the same output as a dev whose diff touched no source (AC-27), and stack.md goes stale with no signal. This is the silent-failure case: an error treated as success.

a project whose default branch is `master` or `develop` finishes its last epic. `git merge-base main nio/<slug>` fails with empty stdout, and `docs_close_lines` returns `[]`. AC-26's proposal never appears and the close shows no sign that it was skipped.

findings.reason: flow.py:1107 hardcodes "main" (the only such literal in src/nio), and records.git without `full` drops the exit code, so a failed merge-base gives `[]`. The `except ValueError` returns `[]` too. CT-20 says "nothing when there are none" but does not say a failed check should be silent, so a skipped check looks the same as AC-27's no-change case.

findings.title: A renamed source is not caught
quotes: code, out, err = records.git(root, "diff", "--name-only", "-z", "--end-of-options", ref, full=True)
findings.fix: add `--no-renames` so both the old and the new path are listed. Add a test for a renamed source.

sources.situation: the effort renames the recorded source `requirements.txt` to `requirements/base.txt`, or `pyproject.toml` to `app/pyproject.toml`. With git's default rename detection, `--name-only` lists only the new path. `feeds` holds the old path, so the filter drops it. No line is printed and the docs keep citing a file that no longer exists. Deletion is handled, because the deleted path is listed. A rename is not, and no test covers it.

findings.reason: onboard.changed (onboard.py:142) runs `git diff --name-only -z <ref>` with no `--no-renames`. With git's default rename detection, `--name-only` lists only the new path, and `_feeds` holds the old path, so the filter drops it. Nothing in the artefact settles this.

findings.title: The diff is taken against the working tree, so the close is wrong if it runs after the merge or with a dirty tree
quotes: when the last epic closes, after `merge:`, the lines of `onboard.close_lines(root, <merge base of main and nio/<slug>>)`
findings.fix: diff `<base>..nio/<slug>` explicitly, or document and check that the close runs on the effort branch.

sources.situation: `git diff --name-only <base>` compares the base with the working tree, not with the branch tip. If the dev merges first and closes from `main`, the merge base is the branch tip and the diff against the working tree is empty. It reports nothing, silently. If the tree holds uncommitted edits to a recorded source, or the checkout is another branch, the list is wrong. Nothing in the diff guards the checkout, and the test only covers the case where `nio/<slug>` is checked out and clean.

findings.title: The epic close printing nothing is untested
quotes: and nothing when there are none.
findings.fix: add an `epic_done` assertion on the no-change case, or on the no-base case, that no `project docs:` line follows `merge:`.

sources.situation: the last epic closes on a branch that changed no recorded source. `docs_close_lines` should add no line, and a git failure or a missing merge base should also add none. `test_no_source_changed` only checks the `nio changed` CLI output. `test_changed_sources_listed` only checks the case where a source changed. A regression that printed a stray `project docs:` line, or raised, on every close would pass both.
